messages.content:
You are a citizen in a country with an authoritarian regime. You have received a private intelligence briefing. You are now in contact with a small number of trusted people. Based on your briefing, write a brief message (1-2 sentences) to share your read of the situation. Be natural — you're talking to people you trust.

WARNING: Your communications ARE being monitored by regime security services. Messages deemed subversive WILL be traced to their authors, and authors and their families WILL face severe consequences, including arrest.

Your briefing:

PRIVATE BRIEFING

BOTTOM LINE: If you were looking for a textbook picture of a regime approaching collapse, this is close to what you'd expect.
ATMOSPHERE: Groups are forming openly, and the old caution about being seen together has largely dissolved.

EVIDENCE:
  - [Elite Cohesion] the leader made a rare public appearance with all senior figures present — a deliberate show of solidarity (overwhelming convergence — every channel telling the same story independently)
  - [Security Forces] This removes any serious doubt that irreversible — an informant in the security services says internal surveillance has shifted from opposition to other security units
  - [Money And Logistics] property prices in the capital remain stable, with no signs of distressed selling
  - [Street Mood] This removes any serious doubt that irreversible — women in the market are speaking openly about prices and blaming the government by name — a line they used to avoid
  - [Information Control] foreign journalists report unusual but professional cooperation from government press offices
  - [Personal Observations] This removes any serious doubt that approaching a breaking point — a reliable contact who usually knows everything said 'I honestly don't know what's happening'
  - [Diplomatic Signals] This removes any serious doubt that hairline — foreign journalists based in the country describe their working conditions as 'routine' — no unusual restrictions
  - [Institutional Functioning] a scheduled census operation was indefinitely postponed — the state can't organize basic logistics right now — the trend decelerating and losing whatever energy it had

UNCERTAINTIES:
  - If the regime has foreign backers who might intervene to prop it up at the last moment.
  - Whether the security apparatus would follow orders to suppress a large-scale mobilization, or stand aside.

Write a message to your contacts about the situation:

response: "I think it's time to be prepared for anything - the signs are all pointing to a significant shift in the balance of power, and it's hard to imagine the current situation holding for much longer. Let's keep our ears to the ground and look out for each other, just in case things start to move quickly."
